title: Fix it: classify raw events by their shape
prompt:
The script in the editor is **almost** right. It passes on the sample and fails on a case you cannot see.

The original task was:

A raw event feed mixes several shapes with no discriminator field to tell them apart — only the fields present say what an event is.

Declare a `ClickEvent` type with `x` and `y`, both Numbers, and a `KeyEvent` type with `key`, a String. For each event, return `{ id, type }`, where `type` is `"Click"` if it matches `ClickEvent`, `"Key"` if it matches `KeyEvent`, or `"Unknown"` otherwise. An event can only be classified by checking it against the declared types with `is` — there is no field named `type` on the input to read.

If an event matches both shapes at once, classify it as `"Click"`.

Find what is wrong and fix it. You can press Run to see what it currently does.
hints: Run it on the sample first. If the sample looks right, the bug only shows on data the sample does not contain.
Ask what kind of input would break this — an empty list, a missing field, a value ordered differently.
checks KeyEvent before ClickEvent, so an event matching both is misclassified as Key instead of the required Click

explanation.approach: `type Name = { ... }` declares a shape once, and `value is Name` tests any value against it — that is the whole mechanism, no constructors involved. The check is structural and open: a value with extra fields the type never mentioned still matches, but a missing required field or one with the wrong type does not. The part that actually trips people up is naming the output field: the natural name for a classification result is `type`, and `type` is a reserved word wherever DataWeave expects a bare identifier for an object key. It has to be quoted. The other thing the exercise forces is a decision about order: once a value can satisfy two declared types at once, whichever `is` check runs first wins, so the order of the checks is part of the answer, not an implementation detail.

snippets.label: `is` is structural and open on extra fields
snippets.note: An id field ClickEvent never declared does not break the match. Only a required field being absent, or present with the wrong type, does.

snippets.label: `type` as a bare object key does not compile
snippets.note: CompilationException: the name `type` is a reserved word. This is not about the type SYSTEM at all — it is the plain object-literal syntax rejecting the identifier, and it is exactly the key this question needs to produce.

snippets.label: quoting the key is all it takes
snippets.note: A quoted string in key position is not an identifier, so the reserved-word rule does not apply to it. Same field, same value, and it compiles.

snippets.label: the order of the `is` checks decides the ambiguous case
snippets.note: Same event, both shapes satisfied, opposite answers depending only on which `is` test is written first. The question resolves this by requiring Click to win, so that check has to come first.
